title: Establish OKR Delivery Lattice and Cross-Functional Decision Rules
creator: Elena Kim
description: Problem: As multiple teams scale their initiative throughput we lack a clear, operational decision protocol for when to re-scope, de-schedule, or fast-track company-level OKR work. That causes late redistributions of engineering effort and unpredictable delivery windows. Goal: Define and socialize an "OKR Delivery Lattice" (a lattice of commitment states + transition rules) and accompanying cross-functional decision rules (priority matrix, RACI for tradeoffs, and an escalation path) so program managers, PMs, Eng and Design have a single source of truth to guide OKR delivery choices. Acceptance criteria: 1) A one-page lattice diagram and a 3-step decision flow published to Confluence; 2) A set of triage rules (latency/cost/regression thresholds + stakeholder veto rules) adopted by at least 5 active initiatives; 3) A rollout plan for OKR enforcement checks integrated into weekly roadmap syncs and Console dashboard alerts for policy violations.
outcome_metrics: mean days from policy-violation to resolution
number of unplanned scope-shifts per quarter
deliverables: Training session + slide deck for PM/Eng/Design lead reps
notes: This work ties into the Roadmap Guardrails effort and the initiative dependency visualizer. We must coordinate with Engineering reliability on observable thresholds and with Design on expected UX impact windows.
